question: On a circle of radius 7 units, PQ and QR are chords of length 7 units each. What is the length of the chord PR in units?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the chord lengths (7 units) equal the radius (7 units), ΔPOQ and ΔQOR are equilateral triangles.

Thus, each chord subtends a 60° angle at the center, making the total central angle for chord PR = 60° + 60° = 120°.

Using the direct chord length formula: PR = 2 × R × sin(θ/2) = 2 × 7 × sin(60°).

PR = 14 × (√3 / 2) = 7√3 units.

To match the given options, multiply the numerator and denominator by √3: 7√3 × (√3 / √3) = 21/√3 units.

**∴ The correct answer is 21/√3 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the circle (R) = 7 units

Length of chords PQ = QR = 7 units

 
• 
• 
• 
•

• O P Q R 
 
 60° 60° 7 7 7 7 PR = ? 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let O be the center of the circle. The radii OP, OQ, and OR all measure 7 units.

⇒ In ΔPOQ, we have OP = OQ = PQ = 7 units. Thus, ΔPOQ is an equilateral triangle, meaning ∠POQ = 60°.

⇒ Similarly, in ΔQOR, OQ = OR = QR = 7 units. Thus, ΔQOR is also an equilateral triangle, meaning ∠QOR = 60°.

⇒ The total central angle subtended by chord PR is ∠POR = ∠POQ + ∠QOR = 60° + 60° = 120°.

⇒ Applying the cosine rule in ΔPOR:

⇒ PR² = OP² + OR² − 2 × OP × OR × cos(120°)

⇒ PR² = 7² + 7² − 2 × 7 × 7 × (−1/2)

⇒ PR² = 49 + 49 + 49 = 147

⇒ PR = √147 = 7√3 units

⇒ To match the fraction format given in the options, multiply the numerator and denominator by √3:

⇒ PR = (7√3 × √3) ÷ √3 = 21/√3 units

**∴ The correct answer is 21/√3 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Central Angle Theorem for Chords

The length of a chord L in a circle of radius R subtending a central angle θ is directly given by the formula L = 2 × R × sin(θ/2).

Cosine Rule

In any triangle, the square of a side is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides minus twice their product multiplied by the cosine of the included angle: c² = a² + b² − 2ab × cos(C).

Equilateral Triangle Properties

When a chord length is perfectly equal to the radius of the circle, the triangle formed by the chord and the two radii is perfectly equilateral, with all internal angles naturally measuring 60°.
